Not first-class. ChatMessage supports a CachePoint content block which Anthropic/OpenAI providers honor — but framework does not auto-place breakpoints; the developer inserts them.

Built-in ResponseCacheProcessor caches full LLM responses (processLLMRequest returns cached chunks). Anthropic-style cache breakpoints are not auto-managed; you place them in system prompt yourself or via a processor.

No first-party prompt-cache breakpoint controller. Providers (Anthropic) handle cache via their own ChatClient (agent-framework-anthropic sets breakpoints). MAF does not expose a generic stable-prefix knob.

Passes previousResponseId to OpenAI Responses API for server-side caching. Does not manage Anthropic-style cache_control breakpoints. ai-sdk extension caching depends on underlying Vercel AI provider.

Cache breakpoints first-class: CachePoint message part; cache_write_tokens / cache_read_tokens on RequestUsage; provider-specific model-settings flags (e.g. bedrock_supports_prompt_caching). InstructionPart split into static vs dynamic so stable prefix is cache-friendly.

Usage struct exposes cached_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens — observe cache hit rate per turn. No automatic cache-breakpoint placement; configure provider-side caching via provider's additional_params.

Tool results go directly into MemoryAdapter::store_tool_interaction. Only knob is sliding-window size which pushes older messages out. No primitive for stashing or summarizing large outputs.
PostToolUse.updatedToolOutput lets you replace large tool outputs with a summary before the model sees them. No first-party stash-to-filesystem-and-replace-with-budget-summary pattern.

Manual after_tool_call hook to summarize/truncate when over threshold. No filesystem-stash / on-demand-re-read pattern. Skills with RESOURCES disclosure level catalog file lists in prompt; agent fetches contents via separate tool you provide.

Filesystem middleware has file-state dedup (returns fileUnchangedStub when tool re-reads unchanged file). No generic stash-large-tool-outputs-to-disk pattern.
wrap_tool_call can rewrite ToolMessage to summary + pointer; BaseStore is a natural stash backend. No first-party tool-result-clearing primitive.

Not first-class outside of Sandbox Agents. Sandbox Agents have a filesystem workspace where tools can write large outputs to disk and reference them by path. Non-sandbox tools just return their result string to the LLM.
